sections.h2: Which Tennessee counties follow the URLTA
sections.html:
Only the larger counties follow it. The act, found in Title 66, Chapter 28 of the Tennessee Code, reaches counties with more than 75,000 residents by the 2010 federal census. Nineteen counties qualify: Shelby, Davidson, Knox, Hamilton, Rutherford, Williamson, Montgomery, Sumner, Wilson, Blount, Sullivan, Washington, Bradley, Sevier, Madison, Maury, Anderson, Greene and Putnam.

The remaining counties fall under Title 66, Chapter 7 of the Code, starting at section 101. Only four sections of that older law actually apply: section 109 on termination of tenancy, 110 on tenants with disabilities, 111 on service and support animals, and 112 on domestic abuse.

How the two Tennessee landlord tenant regimes differ.
TopicURLTA countiesAll other counties
Governing lawTitle 66, Chapter 28Title 66, Chapter 7 (four sections apply)
Rent grace periodFive days, not counting Sundays and legal holidaysNot covered by those four sections
Late fee cap10 percent of the rent past dueNot covered by those four sections
Notice types14 day, 7 day for repeat violations, 3 day14 day, 30 day, 3 day

Check which column your rental belongs in before you send any notice or promise any date. The county clerk or a local attorney can confirm it.

sections.h2: Written notices a Tennessee landlord sends
sections.html:
In a URLTA county, a landlord facing a material breach can deliver written notice that the lease ends after 14 days unless the tenant cures the problem. A repeat of substantially the same act or omission inside six months permits a seven day written notice. Section 66-28-505 sets out these steps, and a three day notice also exists for violence, threats and unsanitary conditions.

  • Monthly tenancy: either party ends it by written notice delivered at least 30 days before the rent due date the notice specifies (section 66-28-512).
  • Weekly tenancy: written notice delivered at least ten days before the end date.
  • Tenant repairs to cure a breach need a written request from the tenant and written authorization from the landlord before work begins.
  • A holdover who remains without consent once the term ends is open to a suit for possession, back rent and reasonable attorney fees.

The owner must rely on the reasons stated in the notice when the case reaches court. New misconduct after a notice goes out calls for another notice. Subsidized housing requires written notice, and federal rules may differ from state law.

sections.h2: What happens to a lease if the landlord sells the house?
sections.html:
The statute deals with the seller's liability and does not end a tenancy. Section 66-28-305 releases a landlord who conveys to a bona fide purchaser in good faith from liability for later events, once the tenant has written notice of the conveyance and the security deposit has moved to the purchaser. Skip either step and the seller stays exposed.

Section 66-28-302 obliges a landlord to give the tenant who manages the property and who may receive service and notices for the owner, with an address for each. The same section makes that duty enforceable against any successor landlord, owner or manager, so whoever buys a rented house takes on that duty.

  • Tell the tenant in writing that the property changed hands and where the deposit now sits.
  • Hand over to the buyer the lease, the deposit and the tenant's contact details.
  • Call the county clerk or a local attorney to learn what notice your lease and county require before assuming the sale lets you end the lease.

Showings come with limits. Section 66-28-403 says a tenant should not unreasonably refuse entry so the landlord can exhibit the unit to actual or prospective buyers, while barring abuse of that access. The same section lists the only situations in which a landlord may enter without consent, such as an emergency or a court order.

Section 66-28-301 requires URLTA-county landlords to place each deposit in an account used only for deposits, at a bank or lender regulated by Tennessee or the federal government. Tenants learn where the account is when they sign and pay, though the account number stays private.

  • Tenants may inspect the unit for the damage behind any charge, and the landlord may invite them to attend.
  • A landlord who skipped the separate account or the written damage listing may not keep any of the deposit.
  • Damage found later is recoverable only if the landlord spotted it inside 30 days after the tenant left or inside seven days after a new tenant took possession, whichever ends first.
  • When nothing is owed and a refund is due, the landlord sends a refund notice to the tenant's last known address, and if no reply arrives within 60 days the landlord may take the money out of the account.

A seller has to pass the deposit to the buyer to earn the release described above. Put the amount in the closing paperwork so both sides agree on it. A cash buyer who takes the house with the tenant in place receives the lease and the deposit the same way.

sections.h2: How an eviction case moves through court
sections.html:
A landlord files a detainer warrant in general sessions court. Three types exist: forcible entry and detainer under section 29-18-102, forcible detainer under 29-18-103 and unlawful detainer under 29-18-104.

  • Service: the summons can go to any adult found in possession, or to a party named in the lease. Personal service supports a money judgment.
  • Posting: after three attempts on three different dates, documented on the warrant, service can be made by posting a copy on the door and mailing one, at least six days before the hearing. Posting supports possession only, not a money judgment.
  • Continuances: the maximum is 15 days unless the parties agree, the landlord consents, or no court is being held.
  • Appeal: a defendant has ten days to appeal to circuit court and must post bond. A certiorari route to circuit court runs 30 days and needs a meritorious reason and bond.
  • Writ of possession: when the landlord wins, the writ is executed and the landlord restored to possession immediately.

If a defendant appeals without posting the required bond, the landlord does not have to post one to obtain possession. The landlord is also entitled to interest on the judgment from the judgment date if the defendant's appeal fails.

sections.h2: Protections for domestic abuse victims in a rental
sections.html:
The URLTA and the older law use identical wording, in sections 66-28-205 and 66-28-517 for URLTA counties and 66-7-109 and 66-7-112 elsewhere. If domestic abuse is the reason a tenancy could be ended, only the perpetrator may be evicted. The landlord may not evict the victim, minor children or innocent occupants, and the perpetrator stays financially liable.

A landlord may remove the perpetrator from the lease and have the remaining adult tenants qualify for a new agreement. The victim and the other adult tenants must agree in writing not to let the perpetrator return. A tenant who is a domestic abuse, sexual assault or stalking victim can also request release from the lease by written notice, with a release date agreed within 30 days and a copy of either a valid order of protection after a hearing or documents showing a criminal charge.

A seller whose tenancy involves an order of protection should get legal advice before serving any notice.

faqs.q: Does the URLTA apply in my Tennessee county?
faqs.a: It applies in counties with more than 75,000 residents under the 2010 census. Nineteen counties qualify, including Davidson, Shelby, Knox, Hamilton and Rutherford. If your county is not listed, the shorter Title 66, Chapter 7 law applies, so confirm with your county clerk before sending notices.

faqs.q: How much notice ends a monthly rental?
faqs.a: In URLTA counties, section 66-28-512 asks for written notice at least 30 days before the rent due date the notice names. A weekly rental needs ten days. For other counties the notices are 14, 30 and three day, so match the notice to your situation.

faqs.q: Can a Tennessee landlord charge a late fee?
faqs.a: In URLTA counties, yes, a fee of up to a tenth of the rent past due, and only after the five day grace period. The grace period does not count Sundays or legal holidays. No late fee cap is listed for other counties, so check your lease.

faqs.q: Does selling the house cancel the tenant's lease?
faqs.a: No statute says so. Section 66-28-305 only frees a seller from later liability after the tenant gets written notice and the deposit goes to the buyer. A local attorney or the clerk can tell you what notice your county expects before you end a lease.

faqs.q: How long does a Tennessee eviction take?
faqs.a: No single timeline is set. Posted service must happen at least six days before the hearing, continuances are limited to 15 days, and a tenant has ten days to appeal. If the tenant appeals without bond, the landlord can still obtain possession.
